newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Plessey warning catches players unawares.
newsitem.headline: Plessey warning catches players unawares.

text.p: Shares in Plessey Corporation Ltd fell on Friday on a profit warning issued shortly before noon, catching some players by surprise.
Plessey issued a warning on the Jet trading system at 0910 GMT that it expected second half earnings to be below those of the first half and for the previous year.
"Everything started falling when the company put out the profit warning. I was a buyer all the way down thinking it was looking cheap," one trader commented.

"When they won the Eastern Europe meter contract the share price did not budge," he added, referring to an announcement by the group on Wednesday that it had won an Eastern Europe meter contract which would be worth eight million rand in the first year.
At the time of its interim results last November, the company said it anticipated an improved performance in the second half of the year.
John Temple, chief executive of Plessey, told Reuters the market seemed to anticipate a profit warning after the group issued a cautionery on February 10 related to the sale of its unit Tek.

"Everybody seemed to think we would issue a profit warning after we made that announcement. They put two and two together and said if they are selling that business it must be because they are losing money," he said.
One analyst said she heard a rumour last week in the market that results would be poor and phoned management which confirmed the rumour.

On Friday, Plessey closed down three percent, or 24 cents, at 776 cents in a volume of over 300,000 valued at over 23 million rand. The group's shares have fallen 224 cents since February 11 when they were quoted at 1,000 cents each.
Plessey said the reasons for the expected fall in results were that the sale of a non-branded television business unit had been reversed after the purchasers failed to meet their obligations.

"This together with lower sales and margins in the television and audio business had led to worse than expected results in the consumer electronics division," the company said in the cautionary announcement.
It said the future of this division was currently under review.
South Africa's Security Regulation Panel (SRP) said on Friday it had not been alerted to any irregularities in the trading of shares ahead of the profit warning.
"We will probably look into it," said Hermie Engelbrecht, the director of surveillance at the SRP told Reuters.
